content.value_statement: Playwright test suites can become flaky, slow, and difficult to maintain. This skill provides practical patterns for locators, fixtures, page objects, debugging, mocking, and configuration.
actual_capabilities: Explains Playwright configuration for browser projects, reporters, retries, traces, screenshots, and local web servers.
Recommends resilient role, label, text, and test identifier locators with auto-waiting assertions.
Demonstrates page objects, reusable fixtures, authentication state, and isolated test structure.
Shows network response mocking, request interception, error simulation, and delayed response testing.
Covers accessibility audits, visual regression checks, trace inspection, screenshots, and debugging modes.
Includes a page object template, command reference, and read-only project setup checker.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and templates; test execution still requires a configured project and installed browsers.
Examples primarily use TypeScript and may need adaptation for JavaScript projects or older Playwright versions.
The setup checker requires Bash, common Unix tools, package.json, and access to the local Playwright command.
The guidance does not provide complete CI pipelines or detailed component testing workflows.

use_cases.title: Create a first end-to-end test
use_cases.description: Turn a user journey into a structured Playwright test with resilient locators and clear assertions.

use_cases.title: Stabilize a flaky test suite
use_cases.description: Replace fragile selectors and fixed waits with observable states, focused fixtures, traces, and reliable synchronization.

use_cases.title: Design scalable test architecture
use_cases.description: Organize page objects, authentication state, browser projects, network mocks, accessibility checks, and visual baselines.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Playwright test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Playwright test for {scenario}. Recommend resilient locators, auto-waiting assertions, and clear arrange, act, assert steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one existing test

prompt_templates.title: Create a page object
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright page object for {page}. Include typed locators, navigation, readiness checks, common actions, and error-state handling.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose flaky behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this flaky Playwright test and failure evidence. Identify likely timing, isolation, locator, network, or state problems and propose focused fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting with traces and logs

prompt_templates.title: Plan a complete test strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Playwright strategy for {application}. Cover browser projects, fixtures, authentication, network mocking, accessibility, visual regression, debugging artifacts, and parallel execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for a production suite

output_examples.input: Review a login test that uses CSS selectors and fixed delays.
output: Replace structural CSS selectors with role and label locators.
Remove fixed delays and wait for visible application states.
Keep successful and rejected login paths isolated.
Capture a trace on the first retry for diagnosis.

output_examples.input: Plan reusable authenticated tests for a dashboard.
output: Create a setup project that signs in once and saves authentication state.
Make browser projects depend on the setup project.
Keep account data isolated when tests modify server state.
Verify a dashboard-specific element before each workflow.

output_examples.input: Improve coverage for an unreliable users API.
output: Mock successful, empty, invalid, delayed, and failed responses.
Assert loading, content, empty, and error states separately.
Use targeted response waits only when user actions trigger requests.
Keep mock payloads minimal and relevant to each behavior.

best_practices: Prefer role and label locators that reflect how users perceive the interface.
Assert observable application states and rely on Playwright auto-waiting instead of fixed delays.
Keep tests isolated, preserve useful failure artifacts, and reuse authentication only when account state remains independent.
anti_patterns: Do not depend on long CSS chains, indexes, or implementation-specific markup when accessible locators are available.
Do not use fixed sleeps or networkidle as a general readiness signal.
Do not share mutable accounts, page state, or test data across parallel tests.

faq.question: Which Playwright languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: The examples focus on TypeScript. Most locator, fixture, debugging, and configuration concepts also apply to JavaScript.

faq.question: Can it run my tests automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide command use, but execution depends on the agent permissions, project dependencies, browser installation, and your request.

faq.question: Does it support page objects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a typed template and patterns for navigation, locators, common actions, errors, lists, and tables.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes resilient locators, auto-waiting, specific readiness checks, isolation, traces, screenshots, and controlled network behavior.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility and visual testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates axe-based accessibility audits and Playwright screenshot comparisons for pages and components.

faq.question: What does the setup checker inspect?
faq.answer: It checks local dependencies, configuration, test files, browser caches, TypeScript, ESLint, npm scripts, and common CI files.
